adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration matches category by name via site setting value, so a renamed category causes hosts to silently fall back to uncategorized

adjudication.rationale: In migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, it derives `category_id` by joining `site_settings` to `categories` on `s.value = c.name` for `s.name = 'embed_category'`. This assumes the `embed_category` setting stores the current category *name*. If the category was renamed since the setting was saved, the join returns no rows (or `id` becomes 0), and the migration explicitly falls back to `uncategorized_category_id` when `category_id == 0`, with no warning/error. That matches the finding: renamed category => hosts migrated to uncategorized silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration interpolates host values directly into SQL INSERT statements, so any host string containing a quote raises a SQL error, aborting the migration after the table is created but before site settings cleanup

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration reads host strings from the `site_settings` table and inserts them using string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. If any `h` contains a single quote (or other SQL-special characters), the generated SQL becomes invalid and will raise, aborting the migration mid-way. Since the `DELETE FROM site_settings ...` cleanup happens after the inserts, a failure during insertion would leave the new table created but the old site_settings rows not removed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec covers the migration in any of its paths, including the acceptance criterion that settings survive the migration

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a data migration (20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb) but does not add any spec that exercises it. However, the proposed finding is fundamentally about missing test coverage/acceptance criteria rather than a concrete bug or defect introduced by the code itself. From the diff alone we can verify “no migration spec was added,” but we cannot verify that this constitutes a required correctness problem (many codebases do not unit-test migrations).

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete() action calls this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...), but unlike save() it does not attach a .catch(popupAjaxError) (or any error handler). If the DELETE request fails, the UI will not show an error and the rejection may go unhandled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation regex permits hosts with ports (example.com:8080) but record_for_host compares uri.host (no port) against stored value, so hosts saved with a port can never match and embedding silently fails

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbeddableHost` validation explicitly allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`). The `before_validation` callback strips scheme and path but does not remove the port, so a saved value like `example.com:8080` is possible (and migration can also insert such values verbatim). However `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the referer with `URI(...)` and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. `uri.host` never includes the port (it would be in `uri.port`), so `example.com` will not match a stored `example.com:8080`, meaning such entries can never authorize embedding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec covers a host-with-port; fabricators and specs only use bare hostnames

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s specs/fabricators do not include an example with an explicit port (e.g. `example.com:3000`), but the proposed finding frames this as a defect. That’s not a verifiable bug introduced by the diff—it's a test coverage suggestion. Also, the claim that specs “only use bare hostnames” is not strictly accurate: several specs use full URLs with scheme/path (e.g. `http://example.com`, `https://example.com/1234/45`), even if they end up being trimmed. So the finding is at best a non-defect improvement request and partially misreads the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update just re-renders the fetch and mutates nothing, while the client wires saveChanges() to embedding.update({}), so the 'save changes' requirement is not actually implemented and untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Admin::EmbeddingController#update`, but it does not change any state: it just re-serializes `@embedding` from `fetch_embedding` (which itself always returns `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`), so a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` has no effect. On the client side, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which will issue that PUT. There are also no tests covering any update behavior (the controller specs only assert subclassing), so if "save changes" is intended to persist anything, it is not implemented or verified in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingSerializer uses embed: :ids for embeddable_hosts, so the payload carries only ids without side-loaded host objects, while the client iterates embedding.embeddable_hosts expecting full records, causing the admin page to render undefined/blank hosts

adjudication.rationale: The serializer’s `has_many :embeddable_hosts, ... embed: :ids` is intentional and is supported by other changes in the diff. `embed: :ids` typically means the relationship on the parent is represented as `embeddable_host_ids` while the full `embeddable_hosts` objects are side-loaded in the same payload. The client store was explicitly updated to hydrate `*_ids` arrays (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/` and mapping to `pluralize(subType)`), which is exactly what’s needed so `embedding.embeddable_hosts` becomes an array of full records. So the claim that the payload carries “only ids without side-loaded host objects” (and thus the admin page would render blanks) is not a verifiable problem from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: before_validation calls self.host.sub! on a possibly nil host with no presence validation, so a request with host: nil causes a NoMethodError 500 instead of a validation error
Controller reads params[:embeddable_host][:host] without require/permit, so a malformed payload without the embeddable_host key returns a 500 instead of a 400

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code directly does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]`. If the request payload omits the `embeddable_host` key (or it is not a hash), `params[:embeddable_host]` will be `nil` (or non-indexable) and `[:host]` will raise `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500. There is no `require(:embeddable_host)` / guard to turn this into a controlled 400-style error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The contents of spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb and spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped: the embeddable host fabricator is in category_fabricator.rb and the category fabricators are in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, causing misfiled work and risk of silently breaking the spec suite when either file is edited or deleted

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` no longer defines `Fabricator(:category)` (and related category variants); instead it defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`. Conversely, the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). This is a verifiable swap/misnaming in the diff and is a real defect in test support code organization that can break specs if files are required by name or modified/removed based on their expected contents.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:3 uses embed: :ids but the admin UI (embeddable-host.js.es6 and embedding.hbs) expects full host objects with host name, category, and isNew/save methods; hydrating embeddable_host_ids yields records with only an id and no client model for embeddable-host exists, so the table renders empty rows or errors

config/routes.rb:138 and app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:16 define a no-op update endpoint: PUT 'customize/embedding' re-serializes a fetched OpenStruct without persisting anything, the client's saveChanges() sends embedding.update({}), and saveChanges isn't wired to any button, creating a dead save path that implies a save-settings flow that doesn't exist

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff adds `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` (config/routes.rb) but `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` merely re-serializes the pre-fetched `@embedding` OpenStruct and does not persist anything (it doesn’t even read params). On the client, `admin-embedding` controller defines `saveChanges()` that calls `embedding.update({})`, but the provided `embedding.hbs` template has no button/action that triggers `saveChanges`; instead, saving happens via `host.save(props)` in the `embeddable-host` component. So the PUT endpoint + saveChanges action form an effectively dead/no-op “save” path in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic.rb:869 deletes the embeddable_hosts guard from expandable_first_post? while its test is kept vacuously, so first-post expansion now activates with zero EmbeddableHost rows, changing truncation/expansion behavior independently of configured hosts without stated intent

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (app/models/topic.rb). Since `embeddable_hosts` site setting is removed/migrated to the `EmbeddableHost` table, this removes the only guard that effectively disabled first-post expansion when embedding was not configured/enabled. As a result, any topic with a `TopicEmbed` will now be considered expandable whenever `embed_truncate` is enabled, even if there are zero `EmbeddableHost` rows (i.e., embedding is effectively disabled for new embeds). That behavior change is directly verifiable from the diff and is a plausible regression in the “disable embedding by clearing hosts” scenario.

Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does:

execute("... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i

If the query returns 0 rows (e.g., the embed_category site_settings row doesn’t exist, or its value doesn’t match any categories.name), execute(...)[0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The intended fallback `if category_id == 0` is never reached in that case.

The “fallback migrates all hosts to Uncategorized” part is directionally true (it would assign uncategorized_category_id when category_id is 0), but in the missing-row case the code crashes before that fallback can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb interpolates #{h} values unescaped into the INSERT statement, risking SQL injection or breakage

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation:

execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"

`h` comes from the existing `site_settings` value `embeddable_hosts` and is inserted unescaped inside single quotes. If any stored host line contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacters, the migration can break or allow unintended SQL execution during migration. This is a verifiable defect in the diff (should use parameterization/quoting, e.g. connection.quote).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:4 vs :16: the validation regex allows ports and before_validation doesn't strip them, so hosts can be saved as example.com:8080, but record_for_host matches on URI#host which excludes the port, so embedding from hosts saved with a port is silently denied

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the validation regex explicitly allows an optional port (e.g. ":8080"), and the before_validation only strips scheme and path (sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '') and sub!(/\/.*$/, '')) but does not remove a port. So a record can be saved as "example.com:8080". However, record_for_host(host) parses the incoming URL via URI(host) and then uses uri.host for lookup, which excludes the port (returns "example.com"). The query where("lower(host) = ?", host) will not match a stored "example.com:8080", causing EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? to return false and embedding to be denied for a host that was configured with a port.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:20: a missing host param causes NoMethodError 500 because before_validation calls self.host.sub! on nil (validates_format_of skips nil values), instead of returning a validation error

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the `before_validation` callback unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice. If `host` is `nil` (e.g., `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is missing or null in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host), this will raise `NoMethodError` before validations run, resulting in a 500 instead of a validation error. The finding’s note that `validates_format_of` “skips nil values” is inaccurate, but the nil `sub!` crash is a real defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1240-1250 contains unrelated drive-by cleanup of digest specs, adding review noise and obscuring what the PR actually touches

adjudication.rationale: The referenced changes in `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` replace `topic = Fabricate(...)` with just `Fabricate(...)`, which is a minor cleanup removing unused local variables. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb and spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains the embeddable_host fabricator while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category fabricators, breaking the file-name-to-fabricator correspondence

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` and the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines the `:category` (and variants) fabricators, so the contents are effectively swapped relative to filenames. However, this is not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone: Discourse/RSpec fabricators are typically loaded by requiring all files under `spec/fabricators`, and fabricator resolution is by fabricator name, not by filename. Since both `:category` and `:embeddable_host` fabricators still exist somewhere in that directory, there’s no clear breakage demonstrated here—just a naming/organization inconsistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb creates the host column with no UNIQUE (or any) index, allowing duplicate rows for the same host and making record_for_host resolve referers to an arbitrary duplicate, making target category assignment nondeterministic

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with `host` and `category_id` but adds no index (and no unique constraint) on `host`. The model `EmbeddableHost` also does not validate uniqueness of `host`. As a result, duplicate rows for the same host are allowed. Lookup uses `record_for_host` -> `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, and `TopicEmbed.import` uses the returned record’s `category_id` to choose the category. With duplicates present (potentially with different `category_id`s), which category is chosen depends on which matching row `first` returns, making the mapping ambiguous and potentially incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:16 uses lower(host) matching via URI.host which strips the port from the referer, but the validation regex permits and stores hosts with ports (e.g. example.com:8080), so stored hosts with ports can never match a referer and host_allowed? silently returns false forever

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host`, which excludes the port, and matches with `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. However, the model’s validation regex allows `:port` and the `before_validation` normalization only strips scheme and path (not `:port`), so a stored value like `example.com:8080` can be persisted but will never match an incoming referer/url because lookup compares against `example.com` (no port). This makes `host_allowed?` incorrectly return false for port-qualified stored hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:3 belongs_to :category has no foreign key constraint and no dependent cleanup path, so deleting the referenced category leaves orphaned category_id values and TopicEmbed.import breaks or lands nowhere silently

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces EmbeddableHost with `belongs_to :category` and a `category_id` column declared `null: false` in the migration, but there is no DB foreign key added and no Rails-level cleanup/constraint (e.g., `dependent:` on the Category side, or validation that the category exists). The admin controller also assigns `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` without checking the referenced category exists. As a result, deleting a Category (or supplying an invalid category_id) can leave embeddable_hosts rows pointing at non-existent categories (orphaned `category_id`), which can then be used by `TopicEmbed.import` (`category: eh.try(:category_id)`) to create topics with an invalid/missing category reference. The exact runtime behavior of PostCreator in that case is not shown here, but the orphaned-reference risk itself is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:3 serializes embeddable_hosts with embed: :ids but no side-loaded records are included in the payload, so the admin page's _hydrateEmbedded lookup produces an array of undefined/blank objects in embedding.hbs; also the plural branch lacks the 'if (hydrated)' guard present in the singular branch, making 'hydrated || []' dead code

app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:14-16 update action renders a serialized success payload without persisting anything, creating a phantom save path that reports success on PUT /admin/customize/embedding

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action (`def update ... end`) only calls `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads params or persists any changes. Since the route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` was added and the Ember controller action `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, a PUT request will return a success payload identical to `show` even though nothing is actually saved. This is a real correctness issue (a no-op update endpoint that appears to succeed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1401-1404 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test passes for the wrong reason because production code no longer checks the host and embed_truncate defaults to false, so the named invariant is never exercised

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:11-13 before_validation calls self.host.sub! which raises NoMethodError on nil host, and with no presence validation or param guard in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host, a missing host produces a 500 instead of a validation error
matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that EmbeddableHost's before_validation uses self.host.sub! and will raise NoMethodError when host is nil, which is exactly the golden issue (nil host causing crash in the callback). Extra notes about controller/validation don’t change the core match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The admin embedding update endpoint is a no-op: update action renders serialized data without persisting anything, yet it's wired to the route and client saveChanges() call, so callers get a 200 and believe the save succeeded when nothing was written

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddingController`, `update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` (id: 'default', embeddable_hosts: `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`). There is no code path in `update` that reads params or writes anything to the DB or settings. On the client side, `admin-embedding` controller defines `saveChanges()` which calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, and the adapter `admin/adapters/embedding` points updates to `/admin/customize/embedding` (a PUT route is added). So a caller invoking saveChanges (or any PUT to that endpoint) will get a successful serialized response without any persistence actually occurring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The data migration is one-way and lossy: it maps old embed_category setting to per-host rows by exact category name match, falls back to uncategorized_category_id on mismatch, then unconditionally deletes the site_settings rows, destroying the original value with no warning if the mapping fails (e.g., slug or renamed category)

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration derives category_id by joining site_settings.value to categories.name for s.name = 'embed_category'. If that exact name match fails, it sets category_id to 0 and then falls back to uncategorized_category_id. After inserting rows, it unconditionally executes `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`, so any original embed_category value is lost even when mapping failed, making the migration effectively lossy/irreversible in that scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb replaces SiteSetting.embed_category with a category lookup based on record_for_host(url) against the article/feed URL host, while ensure_embeddable authorizes against the referer host, so URL/referer host mismatch or feed_polling_url on a different host yields nil and topics silently land in the default category instead of the previously configured embed_category

topic.rb expandable_first_post? removed the embeddable_hosts.present? guard, so with zero embeddable hosts configured topics with a TopicEmbed row still expand; the rewritten spec no longer tests what it claims (it passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` condition from `Topic#expandable_first_post?`, but the `embeddable_hosts` site setting is also removed entirely in this change (migrated to the `EmbeddableHost` model/table). So the old guard can’t remain as-is, and there’s no clear evidence in the diff that “no configured hosts” should disable expansion for already-embedded topics. The claim about the rewritten spec “no longer testing what it claims” also isn’t verifiable from the provided diff snippet (the `expandable_first_post?` spec changes are truncated), so it can’t be confirmed here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator files have swapped contents: category_fabricator.rb defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all the category fabricator definitions, an unexplained shuffle that will confuse future contributors

If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The store.js.es6 regex change to /(.+)_id(s?)$/ rewrites payload handling for every model: any *_ids key is deleted and replaced under its pluralized name, silently removing the attribute from hydrated records for consumers that read xxx_ids (e.g., badge_ids, user_ids), a cross-cutting change shipped solely to support singular category_id

SQL string interpolation of untrusted setting value into raw INSERT in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:22 — host values from the free-text setting are interpolated without parameterization or quoting, causing migration failure on values containing single quotes and enabling SQL injection; fix with parameterized insert/binding

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration reads the old site_settings value for 'embeddable_hosts', splits it into lines, and then builds raw SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If any host line `h` contains a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters), the SQL can become syntactically invalid and the migration can fail. Because the value is interpolated directly into SQL without escaping/binding, it also creates an SQL injection vector against the migration execution context (even if the source is an admin-controlled setting).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unguarded destroy on possibly-nil lookup in app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:17-19 — EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first can return nil for a nonexistent id, and calling host.destroy raises NoMethodError resulting in an unhandled 500

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `host.destroy`. If no record exists for the given `params[:id]`, `first` returns `nil`, and calling `destroy` on `nil` will raise `NoMethodError`, producing an unhandled 500. There is no guard (e.g., `return render_not_found if host.nil?`) or use of `find`/`find_by!` to raise a handled `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same nil-lookup pattern in the update action of embeddable_hosts_controller.rb — save_host(nil) leads to nil.host= NoMethodError

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. If no record exists for that `id`, `host` will be `nil`, and `save_host` immediately dereferences it (`host.host = ...`, `host.category_id = ...`), causing a `NoMethodError`. There is no nil check or 404 handling in the diff, so this is a real defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator file contents are swapped — spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb defines the embeddable_host fabricator and spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the category fabricator

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was changed to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` and a new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` was added containing the `:category` (and related) fabricators. However, this is not inherently a verifiable defect from the diff alone: Fabrication fabricators are typically loaded by globbing all `spec/fabricators/**/*.rb`, so the fabricators will still be defined and usable regardless of which file they live in. The finding points out an odd/misleading file naming mismatch, but it’s not clearly a functional/correctness problem proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6:228 — the /fruits/:id mock unconditionally returns fruits[0] regardless of the requested id, making the renamed store test a tautology that never exercises id routing or hydration of fruit 2's payload

The diff is about embedding/embeddable_hosts and related adapters/controllers/models/migrations/specs. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1403 — the 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test has no setup (no embeddable host fabricate, no embed_truncate setting), so it passes vacuously because embed_truncate? defaults to false, leaving the removed host-gating behavior change with zero test coverage

spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:3 and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:3 — the only tests for the new admin endpoints merely assert controller inheritance and verify no behavior, leaving untested failure modes including EmbeddableHostsController#destroy crashing with NoMethodError on a bad id and Admin::EmbeddingController#update silently not saving

adjudication.rationale: The two new controller specs only check subclassing and do not exercise any endpoint behavior. In the added Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy, it does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `host.destroy`; if the id is invalid/missing, `host` is nil and this will raise `NoMethodError` (real crash path visible in the diff). In the added Admin::EmbeddingController#update, it simply re-renders the serialized @embedding and never applies/saves any incoming params, so a PUT to /admin/customize/embedding is effectively a no-op (silent non-saving behavior is directly shown in the diff). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:192-204 — the new plural-hydration error path is untested; hydrated is a .map() result so || [] is dead code, unresolvable ids silently produce undefined entries with the original *_ids key deleted (unlike the singular branch which keeps obj[k]), and no test covers an unresolvable color_ids entry

adjudication.rationale: In store.js `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/` with `m[2]`) always does `obj[k].map(...)` and then unconditionally `delete obj[k]`, even though `_lookupSubType` may return `undefined` for some ids. That will leave `obj[pluralize(subType)]` as an array containing `undefined` entries and removes the original `*_ids` field, unlike the singular branch which only deletes `obj[k]` when hydration succeeds (`if (hydrated) { ... delete obj[k]; }`). This is a concrete behavioral inconsistency introduced by the diff and can break consumers expecting either valid hydrated objects or the original ids to remain when hydration fails. Also, `hydrated || []` is indeed redundant because `.map()` returns an array (truthy) when called successfully.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration backfill inserts raw, un-normalized host strings, so previously-working scheme-qualified or path-qualified hosts silently stop matching after cutover (raw SQL bypasses the model's before_validation normalization)
matched_golden_ids: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that the migration backfill uses raw SQL to insert host strings without running the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so existing entries containing schemes or paths may no longer match the new bare-host lookup and embedding configs could break. Candidate captures the same underlying issue and impact.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped string interpolation of host values into SQL; any host containing a single quote produces broken SQL and aborts the migration
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core problem: host values are directly interpolated into an SQL string without proper escaping/parameter binding. The candidate emphasizes broken SQL when quotes appear, which is a symptom of the same unsafe interpolation that also enables SQL injection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration is irreversible: def change contains non-reversible execute/DELETE steps with no down method, and the DELETE destroys the site_settings source-of-truth rows without any backup/export, breaking rollback and old-code fallback

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses `def change` but performs multiple non-reversible SQL operations via `execute`, including inserting derived rows into `embeddable_hosts` and a destructive `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. Because these `execute` statements (especially the DELETE) are not wrapped in a `reversible` block and there is no explicit `down` method, Rails cannot automatically rollback this migration, and rolling back the code would also leave the legacy `site_settings` rows missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_category backfill assumes the setting stored the category name; if it stored a category ID (or the category was renamed), category_id resolves to 0 and all hosts silently fall back to Uncategorized
Setting removal (contract) and table creation (expand) land in the same deploy step with no compatibility window, causing old pods to error on missing SiteSetting during a rolling deploy

adjudication.rationale: The diff migrates embedding allowlist data from SiteSetting to a new `embeddable_hosts` table and then permanently removes the old settings in the same migration (`execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`). At the same time, the Ruby code switches runtime checks from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` / `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`. In a rolling deploy where the migration runs before all old app servers are drained, old pods will still execute the previous logic (e.g. `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` previously raised if `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?`), but the migration has deleted that DB setting, making it blank and causing requests to start failing until all pods are updated. This is a real deploy-compatibility problem introduced by the diff (no compatibility window).
